web/testing#

Calls a route table the way HttpClient calls a server, without a network (#85).

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let client = WebTestClient(routes);
let page = await client.get("/notes/7");
test.is(page::Head::code, 200);
test.is((await page.json()).text("title"), "Tea");

Description#

Calls a route table the way HttpClient calls a server, without a network (#85). A request goes through the routes, their arounds and exception scopes, and comes back as the ClientResponse a real client gets, so a test reads it the same way:

A target is a path with an optional query, "/notes?limit=5". The request comes from 127.0.0.1 over HTTP/1.1. A HEAD response has no body, as on the wire, and an accepted WebSocket upgrade is 101 Switching Protocols.

Every method takes headers. A client made with a cookie jar keeps the cookies the replies set and sends them back, as a browser does, so a login and the requests after it can be tested end to end:

let client = WebTestClient(routes: routes, cookies: MemoryCookieJar());
await client.post("/login", FormBody(...));
test.is((await client.get("/me"))::Head::code, 200);

The site of those cookies is http://127.0.0.1; a Cookie field the caller sets is sent as it is, instead of the jar's.
